prompts.midnight_atlas:
Use case: ui-mockup. Direction name: Midnight Atlas.
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing. Create ONE cohesive visual direction for a paired website ecosystem, not multiple alternatives. Canvas 3072 x 2048, two naturally proportioned desktop webpage previews side by side, each designed as a 1440px-wide page, with generous outer spacing. Left is anyps5.cc portal homepage; right is anyps5.games compatibility search homepage. No browser chrome, device frames, perspective or labels outside the webpages. Current date October 11, 2026. Realistic readable UI.
Audience: PC gamers researching the early-stage AnyPS5 PS5 executable porting project. Independent community guide, never imply official affiliation or all PS5 games playable.
Style: exquisite dark editorial gaming reference publication. Near-black navy base, off-white typography, restrained electric lime accent for primary actions; amber for experimental results. Strong oversized grotesk headlines, small monospaced PPSA IDs, airy columns, thin dividers. No purple gradients, glass cards, charts, fake metrics or generic SaaS bento blocks. Fonts at most two; 16px body. Crisp polished flat webpage UI.
Left: compact wordmark ANYPS5.CC, nav Get started / Downloads / Updates, language English. Small understated Community guide line. Large left-aligned headline "Start with what works." Supporting copy "Understand AnyPS5. Set it up. Check your game." Primary action "Get started", secondary "Explore game compatibility". To right, an intentional atmospheric monochrome abstract real raster illustration of executable pathways/PC graphics, elegant and low contrast, no PlayStation logo or console likeness. Lower section editorial numbered steps Check your game / Get the tools / Set up your files and a small latest-updates row, date Oct 11, 2026. Footer "Independent community resource".
Right: matching wordmark ANYPS5.GAMES, nav Compatibility / Test reports; clear large heading "Does your game run?" Large real search field placeholder "Search games or PPSA ID". Compact Windows / Linux and All results chips ONLY. Below one grouped table with lightweight separators, headings Game / Platform / Result / Evidence. Rows: Dreaming Sarah, PPSA02929, Windows, "Playable", "Official table"; Silt, PPSA03306, Windows, "In-game · local patches", "Community report"; Astro Bot, PPSA21564, Windows, "Gameplay with issues", "Community report". Never say Silt or Astro Bot officially playable. Add an elegant featured Dreaming Sarah landscape illustration thumbnail that reads as original art, not a claimed actual screenshot. A discreet explanatory line "Results depend on build, hardware and patches." Source-review date Oct 11, 2026.
Focus each webpage on hero use case and one primary action; don't crowd with feature inventories. Separate through whitespace then dividers; avoid card-inside-card, boxed app containers, excessive badges. Body text comfortable 65-character reading width. ONE consistent style across both surfaces.
prompts.clear_signal:
Use case: ui-mockup. Direction name: Clear Signal.
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, purposeful spacing. ONE cohesive visual direction for the paired independent community sites anyps5.cc and anyps5.games. Canvas 3072 x 2048, two side-by-side naturally proportioned 1440px-wide desktop homepage previews. No browser chrome, frames or perspective. Exact current date October 11, 2026.
Style: sophisticated light technical reference, white / very pale grey, ink navy typography, restrained cobalt blue primary actions, gentle emerald only for officially playable, amber for experiments. A confident Swiss editorial grid, thin navy rules, plentiful whitespace, compact legible tables and sharp simple controls, mostly flat. Font Inter plus monospaced IDs, 16px body. No SaaS bento grids, no card-in-card, no grand fictional statistics or invented metrics. Clean small icon-library-like icons.
LEFT ANYPS5.CC: slim nav Guides, Downloads, Updates, language English. Main headline "A clearer path to AnyPS5." Small copy "Independent guides for setup, downloads and troubleshooting." Primary "Read the setup guide" with Windows/Linux choices. On right, a beautifully typeset three-line real command preview: "relinker --windows input.elf app.exe", "Place system libraries in libs/", "Keep game resources in app0/". Show unobtrusive note "Experimental project. Check your game first." Below spacious two-column editorial section: Get started in three steps (Check compatibility, Choose a release or source build, Follow the OS-specific guide), and "What can I play?" ONLY Dreaming Sarah official Windows source, links "See hardware-specific results". Bottom one real update "v0.1.1 · Sep 28, 2026", descriptor "Official release · newer main builds may differ". No other version anywhere. Footer community and source links.
RIGHT ANYPS5.GAMES: matching header, neutral title "Game compatibility, with evidence." Main search field "Game name or PPSA ID", button Search. Below a dense-but-airy grouped reference table, columns Game, Windows, Linux, Source. Row Dreaming Sarah PPSA02929: Windows "Playable · official table"; Linux "Unverified"; source "Upstream documentation". Row Silt PPSA03306: Windows "In-game · local patches"; Linux "Report available"; source "Community discussion". Row Astro Bot PPSA21564: Windows "Gameplay with issues"; Linux "Experimental report"; source "Community discussion". Never show FPS unless specific hardware bound. Row status strings readable and not giant bright pill badges. Small selected row expansion for Dreaming Sarah shows "60 FPS · GTX 1050 Ti / i5-7500" and "36 FPS · Intel HD 620 / i5-7200", with sentence "Source does not specify test date or build." Footer "Source reviewed Oct 11, 2026". Keep only these supporting areas.
Design ONE consistent family with a portal tutorial hierarchy on left and a reference database hierarchy on right. Exact titles and dates; don't invent release numbers, counts or broad compatibility promises. Imagery not necessary: use typography and whitespace to make the technical subject approachable. Never invent game screenshots or box art.
prompts.selected_refinement:
Use case: ui-mockup. Edit and refine the ATTACHED selected first Midnight Atlas design, preserving its cinematic navy-and-lime editorial personality and clean paired-site hierarchy. This is ONE refined visual direction, with theme states, not multiple alternative ideas. User requires exact brand capitalization "AnyPS5" everywhere: wordmarks "AnyPS5.cc" and "AnyPS5.games", never ANYPS5, anyps5, Anyps5. Both sites must have BOTH a light theme and a dark theme. Current date October 11, 2026.
Create a polished 3072 x 2048 design board with four actual compact webpage previews in a clean 2-column x 2-row layout. Each frame is 1440 x 900 naturally proportioned; sufficient gutters, no browser chrome or perspective. Top-left AnyPS5.cc dark, top-right AnyPS5.games dark; bottom-left same AnyPS5.cc light, bottom-right same AnyPS5.games light. This is the same layout and content shown in two themes. No option numbers or title captions outside the webpage canvases. Show an explicit Sun/Moon compact theme toggle in every site's header next to the language menu.
Refine original composition: simplify dramatically for short viewports. Keep bold typography, generous whitespace, flat page surfaces, fine separators, restrained lime primary action in dark theme, editorial column layout. Dark: #081017 navy, warm-white text, muted slate secondary, #C1ED50 action with dark text. Light: ivory #F6F7F0, #13202D text, fine grey-green rules, dark forest/ink primary button with small lime accent; lime must never be low-contrast text on white. No gaudy gradients, neon outlines, glass panels or generic bento cards. Body fonts 16px; max two fonts, geometric sans plus small monospaced IDs. Use library-style icons only.
CC content in BOTH themes: header wordmark AnyPS5.cc; nav Get started / Downloads / Updates; English menu and Sun/Moon toggle. Small label "Independent community guide". Large headline "Start with what works." Copy "Understand AnyPS5. Set it up. Check your game." Primary "Get started"; secondary text link "Explore compatibility". On the right of hero use subtle abstract architectural beams/raster atmosphere inspired by the source, less overpowering. Below a single horizontal three-column sequence Check your game / Get the tools / Set up your files with short descriptions. Then one compact factual release row "Official release" / "v0.1.1" / "Sep 28, 2026". DO NOT invent any other release number, especially v0.7.2. Footer "Independent community resource".
GAMES content in BOTH themes: header AnyPS5.games; nav Compatibility / Reports; English menu and Sun/Moon toggle. Headline "Does your game run?" Copy "Find scoped test results and original evidence." Search field "Search games or PPSA ID" with Search primary action. Under search one compact horizontal filter line All results / Windows / Linux. Then a clean grouped compatibility table with 3 rows, columns Game / Platform / Result / Source.
Rows: "Dreaming Sarah", "PPSA02929", "Windows", "Playable", "Official table"; "Silt", "PPSA03306", "Windows", "In-game · local patches", "Community report"; "Astro Bot", "PPSA21564", "Windows", "Experimental", "Community report". Green small status dot only for official row; amber for experiments. Under table line "Results depend on build, hardware and patches." Smaller source-reviewed date "Oct 11, 2026". Remove the fake Dreaming Sarah landscape banner completely. Do not generate any game cover or gameplay image and do not invent screenshots. A quiet abstract atmospheric header background may remain, equally readable in both themes.
Spacing, typography, content hierarchy and controls identical across dark and light. No claimed game-completion tests, large made-up counts or generalized 60 FPS promises. Clear, calm, production-quality community reference sites. All four previews legible and balanced.
